chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace:

That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about the payment of a fixed wage (ij'al) for warfare, so he said: 'There is no objection to a man going forth to fight on behalf of another man and taking the wage from him.'

key_terms.أَنْ يَغْزُوَ الرَّجُلُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ: That a man fights on behalf of another man
key_terms.الإِجْعَال: Payment of a fixed wage or stipend

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay someone to fight in jihad on your behalf?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of *ij'al* (fixed wage) in the context of jihad, permitting a man to fight on behalf of another in exchange for a specified payment. This ruling highlights the flexibility of early Shia jurisprudence regarding contractual obligations in religious duties, distinguishing between the spiritual merit of the individual and the communal obligation of defense. It underscores the principle that financial compensation does not invalidate the validity of the act when performed by a capable substitute.
